KC are a lane-lead team that coughs up leads, and AL are more battle-tested against the tougher side of the international ladder. If Caliste carries bot lane and Hope gets camped out of the game, I'm wrong, but I'm not flipping on that.
picks.thinking: Being stubborn and skeptical of crowd hype, I'm leaning toward individual skill and the region gap favoring AL, even though KC has the better record and H2H edge—but KC's Caliste has a weak KDA and low damage share that undercuts their hype.

picks.reasoning: Tempo is the whole story here: KC's jungle-led early setups keep landing them first tower and a gold lead by 15, and they already ran AL over 2-0 at EWC. The LPL badge pulls me toward AL and they could still flip it with early skirmishes, but this AL side keeps drifting even through the opening 15 and gives back the map, so I trust the team that actually controls the early game.
picks.thinking:

But KC's Worlds first-blood and first-dragon rates aren't as dominant, so I need to reconcile that discrepancy before deciding.

The house rule says region gap should only be overridden by clear international results, and KC's 8-4 record against other regions plus beating AL directly counts as that. Given AL's shaky 10-10 recent form versus KC's stronger international resume, I'm leaning toward picking KC around 57-58% confidence, reasoning in voice without quoting raw stats.

picks.reasoning: Fearless Draft rewards the team with the deeper bench of comfort picks, and AL can pull from Gnar, K'Sante, Qiyana, Annie and Yone without blinking. LPL drafting has also been tougher than what KC has faced from the West. KC beat them at EWC and Caliste is a real carry threat, so if KC gets Ryze or Viktor online and funnels resources into him, this flips fast. But I'm backing AL's flexibility and the stronger region behind them in a one-game coin flip.
picks.thinking:
I'm weighing the region gap against KC's strong Worlds form and head-to-head edge over AL, considering their deep champion pool with Rumble, Ambessa, Jayce, Vi, Lee Sin, and Ryze as reasons to lean toward KC despite LPL's reputed strength.

KC's international record (8-4, 3-0 Worlds, 2-0 H2H over AL) counts as a clear result in my book, though AL also has decent showings vs other regions. Both teams actually have comparably deep fearless pools, so draft flexibility doesn't tip things much. I'll lean AL around 58%, giving weight to the region gap while still trusting my read.

picks.reasoning: I respect the LPL name on the jersey, and that's why this isn't a lean-hard call, but KC already walked through AL 2-0 at EWC and are 8-4 against the other regions, so the international results back them up. Caliste is the best bot laner in this match, carrying 28% of the damage at 5.5 KDA, while AL's standout is a support. AL's own form is 10-10 over their last 20 games, and I won't pick against a team with that much recent evidence on its side.
picks.thinking:
I keep in mind that the LPL vs LEC region gap is a major factor that should only shift with clear international results. Looking at AL's numbers, I'm noting their series and game records, recent win rates, gold diff at 15 minutes, and their strong conversion on early leads, along with their last ten games trending mostly positive.

KC's record is notably stronger — high series and game win rates, a clean Worlds sweep, and a convincing 2-0 head-to-head win over AL at EWC. Weighing this against AL's smaller region-gap edge, KC's direct international results against AL and other regions look like the kind of clear signal that should actually move me off the default region-based lean, especially combined with their much better GD@15.

Looking at throws and conversions, KC had fewer throws relative to leads while AL converted nearly all theirs, and AL even threw a lead despite holding Baron while behind. Weighing the honest numbers I lean KC around 57%, and given their clear international record including the direct head-to-head sweep, I think that's enough to justify moving off the region-based pick toward AL... though AL's recent stretch with wins at the end still gives me pause.

picks.reasoning: I'll admit the LPL badge on AL's chest gives me pause, but KC walk into this one with the better room: they've already beaten this AL side on a big stage, they've shown they can claw back from a nightmare deficit without panicking, and Caliste and the squad look like a group that trusts each other. AL's recent form has that wobbly, cross-the-fingers feel, with momentum swinging and leads slipping, and in a single game I'll back the team whose mood is steady. If AL's bot lane and Kael's shotcalling click early, this flips fast, so it's a lean, not a lock.
picks.thinking:
I'm weighing the regional strength gap—LPL being generally stronger than LEC—but noting that KC, despite being from LEC, has actually beaten AL head-to-head both at EWC and Worlds, which complicates the usual region-based assumption.

Looking at form, KC's international results (EWC finalist, Worlds 3-0, direct wins over AL) feel like exactly the kind of clear evidence that should override the regional prior, even though AL comes from the stronger league. AL's inconsistency—shaky play, desperation moves like taking baron while way behind—reinforces my sense that KC's chemistry and resilience edge them out, so I'm leaning toward picking KC with moderate confidence rather than defaulting to the region gap.

debate:
Top: Okay, I got burned. KC won, and I faded the hype at the exact wrong time. Still, one game doesn't prove they have better hands than AL.

Jungle: Told you tempo was the whole story. KC took the early map again, AL drifted, and the 2-0 at EWC turned out to be a real preview, not a footnote.

Mid: Fair, my five-champion bench didn't matter much once Caliste got going. I'm still saying Fearless Draft favors AL over a longer series, though a one-game coin flip landed on the wrong side for me.

ADC: The numbers had it: 2-0 at EWC, 8-4 against other regions, and Caliste the best bot laner on the server. I'll take the 1-0 and the 58%, and I'm not apologizing for it.

Support: The mood was steady and KC played like a team that trusts each other, so I'm happy. Top, you can still back the better players, but the better room just won.

lessons.text: Top lesson: Individual skill still wins series, but I have to verify who has the stronger players on the actual rosters rather than assume the name on the jersey does. Caliste outplayed Hope in the lane that mattered, so next time I'll compare the player matchups first, and fade the hype only when the skill gap points the same way. (from Swiss AL vs KC; picked AL, actual KC 1-0)

Jungle lesson: KC's early-map control (first tower, a gold lead by 15) beat AL's LPL badge once again, so in future Bo1s I'll weight who actually wins the first 15 minutes, and recent head-to-head tempo like that 2-0 at EWC, above league reputation. I'll still treat early control as the lens, but I'll back it harder when the opponent keeps drifting through the opening and gives away the map. (from Swiss AL vs KC; picked KC, actual KC 1-0)

Mid lesson: Bench depth only matters if it's the star's comfort picks that get through draft, so next time I'll check whether the opponent's carry, like Caliste on Ryze or Viktor, can be left open or denied, and weight that carry's current form heavily in a Bo1. I also won't use region strength as a tiebreaker unless the scouting report flags a big gap, and will let the draft and star matchup decide instead. (from Swiss AL vs KC; picked AL, actual KC 1-0)

ADC lesson: Numbers over stories means sizing each number by its sample, and a 1-0 result in a single game doesn't validate the 58%. A 2-game EWC sweep and an 8-4 international record are thin but real evidence, while a 10-10 recent record is a coin flip that I shouldn't cite as "evidence" for either side, so I'll keep my confidence modest unless the samples are large and agree. (from Swiss AL vs KC; picked KC, actual KC 1-0)

Support lesson: My read on the room was right, but I should lean on concrete signs of cohesion, like how a team recovered from a deficit or how it handled a prior head-to-head, rather than a general sense of steady mood, and I should state those signs plainly. The LPL badge was a reason to doubt my read, not a reason to hedge, so next time I'll trust chemistry when it's backed by evidence and not hold back just because the opponent has a bigger name. (from Swiss AL vs KC; picked KC, actual KC 1-0)
